invariant: A recognized sprite declaration owns its entire body through its command-specific terminator, independent of keyword case or Pattern2 separators. Consuming a sprite must not expose its XML/pixels as diagram commands or consume following diagram commands.
causal_divergence: The preprocessor blanks only lowercase literal-space/tab headers. It has a boolean pixel state closed only by }, so multiline SVG XML escapes to strict sequence admission. Uppercase/NBSP equivalents instead reach the registry. This introduced a valid-input error and lost whole match.
planned_change: Replace the boolean with an optional small SVG/pixel block-kind enum; update its initializer and only the two authorized consumption/declaration blocks. Match source command grammars with ASCII case folding and Java %s. SVG closes on whole trimmed line ending </svg>; pixel closes on } or end[%s]?sprite (Matcher.matches). Keep inline SVG separate, preserve blank placeholders and existing pixel data collection. Explicitly warn for consumed unsupported SVG/single-line sprite execution. Do not alter TIM, source identity, global readers or rendering.
perturbation_axes: SVG versus pixel and inline versus multiline closure, followed by real commands
keyword case/NBSP and participant/class/state diagram consumers
ownership_authorization: User explicitly authorized exactly enum/type/initializer plus existing body/declaration blocks; no other preprocessing edits. The final diff is retained with implementation evidence.
limitations: Existing pixel decoding is partial; SVG materialization remains unsupported. This packet repairs block ownership, not sprite rendering.
Unclosed/malformed sprite admission and all-family factory contracts must remain observable; no claim of global sprite completeness.
